Source: http://cjonline.com/

Posted May 18, 2000
(MarijuanaNews note: These two letters to his hometown paper show the arrogance of a man who is accustomed to getting away with lying. Voth is treated with unwarranted respect in Topeka, but even there they are beginning to question the party line.)

May 14, 2000
From The Topeka Capital-Journal
letters@cjnetworks.com
http://cjonline.com/
By Eric A. Voth, M.D. -- Chairman of the International Drug Strategy Institute.
See
The Prohibitionist True Believers Explain What The IOM Report Said --
" Marijuana Causes Health Problems "
and
Classic Reefer Madness from Drug Watch International:
" MARIJUANA USED BY JONESBORO KILLERS "!

LEGALIZATION OF DRUGS IS A DANGEROUS IDEA

Dick Snider is correct about one thing in his April 28 commentary on drug legalization. My response is, to quote him, " Rot, balderdash, nonsense, bilge, and baloney " -- or perhaps something more colorful.

The advocates of legalization are quick to assert that legalizing drugs would reduce crime. I fail to see how; 70 percent of violent crime takes place under the effect of alcohol or other drugs. So how is legalizing drugs going to reduce it? Organized crime groups don't just dry up and blow away, they find other venues.
See
Organized Crime In The Marijuana Trade.
Why More " Law Enforcement " is Counterproductive.
An Excellent Halifax Editorial Says, " Marijuana laws encourage crime. "

In Holland, a country where drug enforcement is lax, the murder rate is three times that of the United States.
(MarijuanaNews note: The murder rate in Holland is less than 25% that of DEAland. Everything else that Voth says is about as close to the truth as that point. Prohibitionists have to lie about Holland.)
See
Drug Bizarro Acknowledges Error On Dutch Murder Rate, But Won’t Apologize, Instead Blames Interpol
and
NORML Director Explains To The Dutch
Why Their Drugs Policy Threatens DEAland Prohibitionists – Great Article
and for the Dutch government's official data see
http://netherlands-embassy.org/fie_hltenv.html

The Dutch have also seen staggering increases in violent crime, and marijuana use among their teens is up 277 percent since the policy changes.
(MarijuanaNews note: This is just nonsense. The " Dutch marijuana use among their teens " rose, but remains below that of DEAland, and many other European countries.)
See
 " The failure of Dutch drug policy " An Examination of Prohibitionist Propaganda and the Official Dutch Government Response -- Special To MarijuanaNews

Australia has twice the heroin-related deaths than a country like Sweden, a country with restrictive drug policy.
See
Sweden Brings Felony Charges Against Anti-Prohibitionist For Drug-Free Hemp Products.
and links.

In Alaska, during its period of marijuana legalization, use of marijuana and other drugs was almost twice that of the rest of the country.
(MarijuanaNews note: Marijuana has never been " legal " in Alaska. It has been -- and in much of the state still is -- legal under state law to possess it in one’s own home, but there has never been a provision for legal sales or possession outside of the home. If the " use of other drugs " really is twice that of other states, then why would the legal status of marijuana matter. The Dutch rate of hard drug use is below that of most other European countries.)

I just returned from Los Angeles after speaking to a large group of state and federal law enforcement officers.

(MarijuanaNews note: That sentence is the one substantively important point. The narks have a quack come in and reinforce the party line. Steve Kubby has written extensively about the fact that many of the California police refuse to obey the state’s medical marijuana law.
See
What Part Of 'Exempt' Do California District Attorneys Still Not Understand?
and
California Narks Lie to Justify Disobeying Prop 215. And They Lie About Me In The Process.
and links
Why? Because people like Voth are there telling them that medical marijuana is " medical excuse " marijuana and just a plot to legalize all drugs for small children, babies and sub-atomic particles.)

They are acutely aware of the surges in drug availability every time drug policy softens.
(MarijuanaNews note: Voth and the narks quote one another.)
See
Comparison of drug addiction levels in various European countries.
and
Final Report Of Dutch National Drug Use Survey Will Require New Lies From The Drug Czar:
Their Lifetime Cannabis Use Half of DEAland’s; Two-Thirds That of UK

They are now extremely concerned about the tremendous influx of MDMA (Ecstacy) from, guess where, Holland.
See
Prohibitionist UK -- Not Holland -- Leads Europe In Illegal Drug Production.
But This Does Not Fit the Prohibitionist Party Line

Functionally speaking, how would we legalize drugs? Only a few? Only certain strengths?
Any type of control would create a black market.
(MarijuanaNews note: Why? How? The black market for alcohol is tiny compared with the black market for illegal products.)
Snider's comment about the government providing drugs wold be a fiasco. Imagine if the government provided any drug that a user desired. Alcohol and other drugs already cost the United States at least $170 billion in lost productivity annually. And finally, look at the effects of our two legal drugs, alcohol and tobacco. Between those two we have around 500,000 deaths annually, 11 million alcoholics. Why would we even think of increasing those numbers and adding other drugs?
See
Great London Times Column and News From New Zealand Compare Marijuana and Alcohol
and
 " Two Drugs Are Quite Enough " NZ Editorial;
Saying Marijuana Is " No Worse Than Alcohol and Tobacco " Won't Work
Our most effective approach to reducing drugs is prevention, but how can you prevent drug use with a nod and a wink?
See
Legalize Marijuana and Reduce Use?
New Survey Puts Estimate of Dutch Marijuana Use Even More Below DEAland

That has been the big problem in controlling alcohol use among teens. You might be interested to know that a new study on the effects of driving under the influence of alcohol and marijuana doubles the effects of alcohol alone. Dick, maybe you ought to start quoting some of the information that I send you so you don't have to share the road with more stoned drivers. (MarijuanaNews note: Marijuana is blamed for making alcohol even worse. Of course, Voth does not say that the same study shows that marijuana has far less effect on driving that alcohol.)
For a mor complete comparison of the effects of the two see
Canadian Study Confirms That Marijuana Impairs Driving Far Less Than Alcohol

ERIC A. VOTH, M.D., chairman, International Drug Strategy Institute.

(MarijuanaNews note: And on hemp…)

March 20, 2000
From The Topeka Capital-Journal
letters@cjnetworks.com
http://cjonline.com/
By ERIC A. VOTH, M.D., Topeka, chairman, International Drug Strategy Institute.

ISSUE IS MARIJUANA

Despite claims that hemp/marijuana has great potential for industrial uses, little potential exists for hemp to be a viable crop. The U.S. Department of Agriculture has re-evaluated the potential uses of hemp and determined that it represents only a small niche market.
See
Add The Agriculture Department To The Institutions Corrupted By Marijuana Prohibition. -- 2 Articles

Evaluations from the University of Kentucky, University of Hawaii, and the International Drug Strategy Institute have found that the international market for hemp is actually declining. Experience from Canada has demonstrated that the increased growing of hemp has resulted in glutted markets.
See
Drug Czar Seeks To Ban All Hemp Products

The hemp movement threatens legitimate farmers by making expansive claims.
(MarijuanaNews note: Whereas they are not " threatened " by laws that make growing hemp a felony?)

It poses a serious risk to farmers who give up legitimate crops like soybeans, corn or fiber alternatives.
(MarijuanaNews note: What a patronizing attitude toward farmers. Do they need some reefer madness quack to save them from freedom?)

Hemp also creates a serious dilemma for law enforcement who are faced with the use of hemp as a decoy for marijuana cultivation and trafficking. Do not forget that hemp is the fiber stalk of the marijuana plant. While the THC concentration in hemp may be low, it still can contain THC.
(MarijuanaNews note: No, hemp is the entire plant, but the restriction on THC applies to the tops, undiluted by the stalks. Otherwise, a large marijuana plant might be legal " hemp. " )
Finally, please remember that most supporters of hemp wear items with a marijuana leaf logo, not a hemp stalk. It is marijuana that they really wish to legalize.
See
Prohibitionist France Largest European Producer Of Hemp; EU Subsidies Reduced.
and
 " A representative for the Campaign Against Marijuana Planting contended Friday
that for every argument made in favor of hemp legalization, there is one against. "
Can They Really Count That High?
